questions: When the board is fully visible, does it hold exactly three pens arranged in a single row?
Are all three pens aligned identically, all pointing the same way, including any pen near the left or right frame edge as it enters or exits?
Do all three pens share identical barrel and cap colors, with no mismatch?
Is every pen fully capped with no exposed writing tip, and are all three pens equal in length?
Does the board advance steadily from left to right at EVERY moment, never halting, freezing, or pausing even briefly (1-3 seconds) at any point in the video?
Do all pens stay fixed in their positions on the board, with no pen shifting, sliding, or moving on its own relative to the board mid-clip?

question_answers.evidence: At 00:09 and 00:10, when the board is fully visible, there are exactly three pens arranged in a row.

All three pens have the dark cap at the bottom (cap-down orientation). Although the rightmost pen is tilted, it satisfies the 'same end down' condition specified in the nominal description, and the specific anomaly definition for wrong orientation refers to being 'flipped' (180 degrees).
All three pens have translucent grey barrels and black caps, appearing identical in color.
All pens show the thick black cap at the bottom end, indicating they are capped. They appear to be of equal length.
The board moves steadily from left to right throughout the clip. The initial frames (00:00-00:01) show the rail before the board enters, which is normal entry, not a mid-travel pause.
The pens remain fixed in their relative positions on the board as it moves.

parsed.reason: The board carries exactly three identical pens, all capped and oriented with the cap down. The motion is smooth and continuous from left to right. The tilt of the rightmost pen is considered a minor variation consistent with the 'same end down' requirement and does not match the specific 'flipped' definition of wrong orientation.
